title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
gist: Minxin Pei argues that of the People's Republic of China's eight premiers, only Zhao Ziyang and the recently deceased Zhu Rongji (d. age 97) deserve credit for the country's economic rise, with Zhu's 1990s reforms building on Zhao's 1980s implementation of Deng Xiaoping's 'reform and opening up' vision.

insights.claim: Of the eight premiers the People's Republic of China has had since its founding almost 77 years ago, only Zhao Ziyang and Zhu Rongji deserve credit for the country's economic rise.
insights.speaker: MINXIN PEI
insights.so_what: Frames China's reform trajectory as dependent on a small number of individual reformist leaders rather than institutional continuity, relevant to assessing how durable current economic policy direction is under different leadership.
insights.quote: since its founding almost 77 years ago, the People’s Republic of China has had eight premiers. But only two—Zhao Ziyang and Zhu Rongji—deserve credit for the country’s economic rise.
insights.locator: Since its founding almost 77 years ago

insights.claim: Zhao Ziyang translated Deng Xiaoping's vision of 'reform and opening up' into concrete policy in the 1980s, pushing through the reforms that underpinned China's economic miracle.
insights.speaker: MINXIN PEI
insights.so_what: Establishes the historical baseline against which later reform premiers, including Zhu Rongji, are measured.
insights.quote: In the 1980s, Zhao translated Deng Xiaoping’s vision of “reform and opening up” into policy, pushing through the reforms that underpinned China’s economic miracle.

insights.claim: Zhu Rongji, who died recently at age 97, accumulated a lengthy list of economic accomplishments in the 1990s and became one of China's most respected senior leaders.
insights.speaker: MINXIN PEI
insights.so_what: Marks the death of a figure credited with 1990s market reforms, a reference point for evaluating China's current reform stalling or acceleration narratives.
insights.quote: In the 1990s, Zhu—who recently passed away at age 97—racked up his own lengthy list of accomplishments, becoming one of China’s most respected senior leaders.

insights.claim: Zhu Rongji's personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would ever rise to the top of Chinese politics, yet he did and then implemented reforms that turned China into an economic powerhouse.
insights.speaker: MINXIN PEI
insights.so_what: Suggests China's most consequential reformers have sometimes been political outsiders, a pattern worth watching when assessing which current officials might drive future reform.
insights.quote: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics.
insights.locator: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges
